pathway.title: Comstock Resources Inc — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Internal cash generation does not fund the investment plan, and that is the central weakness. Capital expenditures were 1.97x operating cash flow in the twelve months to 2026-09-30 and 1.50x in FY2025, and the 2026 plan of USD 1.4 billion to USD 1.5 billion for development and exploration is 1.65x to 1.77x that twelve-month operating cash flow, before USD 100 million to USD 150 million planned for the midstream partnership. Bank borrowings, asset sales and partner capital have met the gap, so debt rises whenever prices do not. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 63; calculation C11

Reported leverage flatters credit quality. Net debt to twelve-month EBITDA is 2.37x as reported but 3.49x after removing sale gains and unrealised hedge gains, which sits just below the bank facility's leverage covenant of 3.5x; the covenant definition is not supplied, so no headroom is inferred. Net debt rose from USD 2,785.14 million at 2025-12-31 to USD 3,338.34 million at 2026-09-30, and pro forma net debt after the sale agreed on 2026-11-04 is not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C15

Interest cover is adequate and rate exposure is small. EBITDA covers cash interest 6.71x as reported and 4.55x on the normalised basis, and only the USD 800.0 million of bank borrowings carries a floating rate, 23.61% of debt principal, while the 2029 and 2030 senior notes carry fixed coupons. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation C5

Liquidity and refinancing risk are manageable until 2028 but rest on one bank facility. At 2026-09-30 cash was USD 18.63 million and undrawn commitments were USD 700.0 million of USD 1,500.0 million, and pro forma figures after the sale of 2026-11-04 are not established. The amendment of that date moved the bank maturity from 2027-11-15 to 2028-11-15, and no other debt falls due before 2029, when USD 1,623.88 million of notes mature, followed by USD 965.0 million in 2030. The issuer's own fair values put the 2029 notes at 99.5% of face and the 2030 notes at 95%. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation C15

Business risk is concentrated in one commodity and one basin, so margins follow the gas price. A 60.10% rise in the realised gas price between FY2024 and FY2025 lifted normalised EBITDA by 21.97% even though output fell 14.67%, and normalised net leverage moved from 3.53x to 2.73x. Cash costs of USD 0.83 per Mcfe are 26.95% of the nine-month 2026 realised price, which leaves room at current prices, but a 10% lower price on twelve-month sales would cut normalised EBITDA by 14.59% and lift normalised net leverage to 4.09x before hedge gains and any cost response. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 58; EX99.1_2026-09-30_crk_crk-ex99-1-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3

Governance risk is medium and does not change the credit view by itself. The majority stockholder has supplied equity and paid no dividend since 2023, but the August 2026 farmout with a stockholder partnership and a minority investor in the midstream subsidiary route part of future cash flow to outside holders, and the terms of both are not supplied. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A)

The sale to SOCAR is the swing factor, and its effect cannot yet be measured. The USD 1.65 billion price is 2.06x the USD 800.0 million drawn on the bank facility and equals 49.43% of net debt at 2026-09-30, and the issuer plans to repay the bank facility and retire part of the 2029 notes, but closing is expected only by the end of 2026 and no source states net debt or the earnings of the interests sold. Until it closes, creditors should rely on the normalised 3.49x. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 30; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C6

runs.text: Unit costs are low against the realised price, which keeps margins positive in weak price years. Cash costs were USD 0.83 per Mcfe in the nine months to 2026-09-30, 26.95% of the realised price, and the issuer states an operating margin of 73%; in FY2024 production costs of USD 0.73 per Mcfe were 36.87% of a USD 1.98 price. Margin therefore moves with price rather than cost, which supports cash generation through a price trough. Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_crk_crk-ex99-1-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 59; calculation C2

Capital spending is largely discretionary, which gives management a lever to protect liquidity. The issuer states that the timing of most future capital expenditure is discretionary because it has few long-term commitments, remaining drilling rig commitments are USD 12.7 million, and capital expenditures were cut 22.99% in FY2024. The lever protects liquidity before it protects earnings, because output was 14.67% lower in FY2025. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C1; calculation C4

The reserve base and operatorship give a long runway and control over timing. About 41% of proved reserves are developed, the reserve life is about 16 years and the issuer operates 99% of proved reserves, so it sets drilling pace and cost; the proved undeveloped volume is price-sensitive, however, because it rose about fourfold in 2025 on the higher gas price used to book it. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 16

Debt is long-dated and mostly fixed-rate. The bank facility matures on 2028-11-15 and the notes in 2029 and 2030, only 23.61% of principal floats, and swaps and collars cover volumes through 2028, so a price or rate shock reaches cash flow slowly. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation C5

Cash generation is the first weakness. Capital expenditures were 1.97x operating cash flow in the twelve months to 2026-09-30, so debt, asset sales or partner capital fund the plan and net debt rose to USD 3,338.34 million at 2026-09-30, with the pro forma figure after the sale of 2026-11-04 not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C15

Price exposure is the second weakness. The business sells one commodity from one basin at index prices, and a 10% lower price on twelve-month sales would cut normalised EBITDA by 14.59% and lift normalised net leverage to 4.09x before hedge gains and any cost response. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation C3

Liquidity rests on one bank facility. Undrawn commitments were USD 700.0 million at 2026-09-30, which would cover about 10.26 months of the twelve-month shortfall between operating cash flow and capital expenditures if no partner capital or sale proceeds arrived, and the extension of the bank maturity to 2031 depends on the sale closing. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation C12

Outside holders hold claims on part of the cash flow. A fund holds a 27% interest in the midstream subsidiary with a minimum return, a stockholder partnership will take later cash flow from 27 wells under the August 2026 farmout, and a majority stockholder controls the vote, so consolidated figures overstate the cash that reaches Comstock's own creditors. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 21

Legal terms are unseen. The rank and security of the notes, guarantors, covenant definitions and the terms of the sale are not supplied, so creditor priority and covenant headroom are not established. Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); Financial foundation (CP-1)

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Three transactions define the period. On 2026-11-04 Comstock agreed to sell SOCAR non-operated working interests in 15% of its Western Haynesville upstream interest, 20% of its other upstream interests and 15% of its interest in Pinnacle Gas Services for USD 1.65 billion, subject to customary adjustments, with an effective date of 2026-07-01 and closing expected by the end of 2026. SOCAR's Western Haynesville interest falls to 7.5% after five years and a 15% return, and the issuer expects a gain of USD 150 million to USD 250 million on closing. The issuer plans to repay the bank facility and retire part of its 2029 senior notes with the proceeds. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 30

On 2026-06-15 Pinnacle Gas Services issued Class A-2 Units equal to a 27% interest to a fund managed by Sixth Street Partners for USD 600 million and used the cash to redeem the earlier partner's interest for USD 445 million; no gain or loss was recognised because Comstock kept control. On 2026-08-31 Comstock agreed a farmout with a partnership owned by its majority stockholder, under which the partnership funds 85% of 18 Western Haynesville wells and 80% of nine Legacy Haynesville wells expected to cost about USD 450 million, and Comstock recovers its costs from the wells' net revenues before the partnership takes the net proceeds until it earns a 15% return, after which 50% of the interest in the subject wells reverts to Comstock. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 21

Comstock has issued no notes since the USD 400.0 million of 2029 senior notes sold in April 2024. In the nine months to 2026-09-30 it borrowed USD 1,047 million on its bank facility and repaid USD 507 million, leaving USD 800.0 million drawn. The amendment of 2026-11-04 extends the bank maturity to 2028-11-15, with a further extension to 2031-11-15 after the SOCAR closing and debt repayment, and commitments stay at USD 1.5 billion. The subsidiary's own facility of USD 150 million was undrawn at 2026-09-30. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 100; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation C8

fields.value: Eight documents are in hand: two annual reports, three quarterly reports and three earnings releases, the latest dated 2026-11-05. Three limits shape what the record can support. The consolidated statements include a midstream joint venture whose bank facility and assets sit outside the senior bank facility's collateral. A pending asset sale and an amended bank facility, both agreed on 2026-11-04, have no pro forma statement in any source. No executed indenture or credit agreement was supplied, so debt terms rest on the filings' summaries.

fields.value: Issuer: Comstock Resources Inc (issuer crk-23194), as of 2026-11-18. Pathway: credit snapshot. Scope: extract and normalise the issuer's financial statements for FY2023 to FY2025 and the nine months to 2026-09-30, and build the debt, liquidity, leverage and coverage tables from the supplied filings and releases.

Net debt rose from USD 2,785.14 million at year-end 2025 to USD 3,338.34 million at 2026-09-30. Interest cover is 6.71x EBITDA to cash interest and 4.55x on normalised EBITDA, but the 2026-11-04 asset sale and bank facility amendment are not in these figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported net leverage fell from 4.62x at year-end 2024 to 2.03x at year-end 2025 and stood at 2.37x on an LTM basis at 2026-09-30, but most of that improvement is not operating. EBITDA (Reported) for FY2024 absorbed an unrealized hedge loss of USD 197.607 million, and FY2025 includes a gain on sale of USD 291.938 million, mainly the Shelby Trough sale, and an unrealized hedge gain of USD 62.402 million. With sale gains and unrealized hedge gains removed, net leverage was 2.86x at year-end 2023, 3.53x at year-end 2024, 2.73x at year-end 2025 and 3.49x at 2026-09-30, so the real improvement was a reduction of about 0.80x in 2025 that has since reversed.

fields.value: Net debt rose by USD 553.199 million between 2025-12-31 and 2026-09-30 while normalised LTM EBITDA of USD 955.578 million is below the USD 1,018.356 million of FY2025. Capital expenditures of USD 1,299.936 million in nine months 2026 exceeded operating cash flow of USD 622.379 million, and the gap was met by net bank borrowings of USD 540.000 million and partner capital, not by retained cash. The reported ratios sit well below the bank facility's leverage covenant of 3.5 to 1.0, while the normalised ratio is close to that level; the covenant definition is not supplied, so no headroom is inferred.

Cover is adequate while the 6.75% notes and 5.875% notes carry fixed coupons, and the floating-rate bank debt of USD 800.000 million at 2026-09-30 is the only part exposed to rate changes; no interest-rate hedge is described.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating cash flow after working capital covered only part of capital expenditures in every period: capital expenditures were 1.40x operating cash flow in FY2023, 1.77x in FY2024, 1.50x in FY2025 and 1.97x on an LTM basis, and operating cash flow fell short of capital expenditures by USD 818.805 million for the LTM. FY2025 spending was funded by USD 428.868 million of asset sale proceeds and USD 215.500 million of partner contributions, and nine months 2026 by USD 1,047.000 million of bank borrowings less USD 507.000 million repaid and USD 600.126 million of partner contributions less a USD 445.000 million redemption. The business therefore depends on continued access to the bank facility and partner capital while it invests above internally generated cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash was USD 18.633 million at 2026-09-30 and undrawn commitments of the Comstock facility were USD 700.000 million, USD 540.000 million lower than the USD 1,240.000 million at 2025-12-31 because net borrowings of the same amount were drawn. The issuer reports liquidity of USD 868.6 million, which adds the undrawn PGS facility of USD 150 million that is restricted to PGS, and its consolidated cash includes PGS cash of USD 16.4 million that is not available for general purposes. At the balance-sheet date the bank facility matured on 2027-11-15, about 13 months away, and the amendment of 2026-11-04 moved it to 2028-11-15, with a further extension to 2031-11-15 only after the SOCAR sale closes and debt is repaid; no other debt matures before 2029. The bank facility commitments of USD 1,500.000 million sit below the borrowing base of USD 2.0 billion, so availability is set by commitments and not by the base.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On 2026-11-04, after the balance-sheet date, the issuer agreed to sell non-operated interests in upstream assets and in PGS to SOCAR for a stated cash price of USD 1,650 million and amended the bank facility to mature on 2028-11-15, with a further extension to 2031-11-15 after the sale closes and debt is repaid. Neither event is in any period figure, and no source states net debt after the sale or the EBITDA of the interests sold, so a pro forma leverage figure is not established; the issuer states that proceeds will repay the bank facility and retire part of the 6.75% notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The redemption of the PGS noncontrolling holder appears with different figures: an agreement for USD 440 million plus accrued unpaid distributions, and a payment of USD 445 million on 2026-06-15 funded by USD 600 million of new units. The cash flow statement figure of USD 445.000 million is used in the tables; the agreement figure, the paid figure and their roles are kept in one conflict row.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No customer deposits, deferred revenue, supplier finance or similar non-interest-bearing funding liability is described in any source, and a search for those terms found none; accounts payable and accrued expenses are ordinary trade and capital-spending liabilities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EBITDA (Reported) is built from components because the issuer states no unadjusted EBITDA, and it includes derivative and sale gains, so it is a measure the issuer does not itself use. The issuer's own adjusted EBITDAX is stated for quarterly and nine-month periods only, so adjusted leverage cannot be stated for a fiscal year or the LTM. Consolidated figures include PGS, whose cash and assets are not freely available to Comstock, and no figures for the group that borrows under the Comstock facility are supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Four gaps are rated high. The missing executed debt documents mean rank, security, guarantors and covenant definitions rest on summaries; the missing pro forma capitalisation means the SOCAR sale, whose stated cash price of USD 1,650 million compares with a carrying value of debt of USD 3,356.968 million, is not reflected in any leverage figure; and the missing adjusted EBITDA for fiscal years and the LTM leaves the issuer's own earnings measure unavailable for leverage. Each gap is listed under Gaps with its severity and the action that would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Amounts are in thousand USD unless stated; the money tables restate them in US$m by dividing by 1,000.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Adjusted EBITDA for the twelve months to 2026-09-30 and for each fiscal year cannot be calculated, because the issuer states adjusted EBITDAX only for quarterly and nine-month periods and no supplied source states it for FY2025 or for the fourth quarter of 2025. The adjusted leverage and adjusted cover rows are therefore not calculable, and the only adjusted bridge covers nine months 2026. The fourth quarter 2025 earnings release or a full-year adjusted EBITDAX reconciliation would close it. Severity: High.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt, leverage and liquidity after the SOCAR sale are not established. The agreement dated 2026-11-04 states a cash price of USD 1,650 million subject to customary adjustments, an effective date of 2026-07-01 and closing expected by the end of 2026, and the issuer plans to repay the bank credit facility and retire part of the 6.75% notes, but no source states net debt after those steps or the EBITDA of the interests sold. Every ratio here is as reported at 2026-09-30. A closing statement or pro forma capitalisation would close it. Severity: High.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The legal rank, security of the notes, guarantors and obligor scope are not stated for the 6.75% senior notes, the 5.875% senior notes or the bank credit facility, beyond the statement that the bank facility is secured by substantially all assets except PGS. The debt stack is therefore not drawn and no secured or senior subtotal is stated. The indentures and the credit agreement, which are named only in exhibit lists, would close it. Severity: High.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Covenant definitions and the issuer-reported covenant ratios are not printed: the filings state a leverage ratio below 3.5 to 1.0 and an adjusted current ratio of at least 1.0 to 1.0 for the bank facility, with compliance at 2026-09-30, but not the ratios or their definitions. Covenant headroom is not inferred. The credit agreement would close it. Severity: High.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Consolidated figures include Pinnacle Gas Services, whose bank facility and assets sit outside the collateral of the Comstock facility; PGS cash of USD 16.4 million and net other property of USD 471.5 million cannot be used for general corporate purposes, and the issuer's reported liquidity includes the undrawn PGS facility. No figures for the group that borrows under the Comstock facility are supplied, so consolidated net debt and leverage may not describe that group. Restricted-group financials would close it. Severity: Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The redemption of the Pinnacle Gas Services noncontrolling holder is described as USD 440 million plus accrued unpaid distributions in the annual report and the first quarter report and as USD 445 million paid on 2026-06-15 in the third quarter report, and the second quarter release says the proceeds also retired preferred equity and indebtedness. The figures are logged in one conflict row and are not reconciled. A reconciliation from the issuer would close it. Severity: Medium.

No action is needed. Severity: Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Issuer: Comstock Resources Inc (issuer crk-23194), as of 2026-11-18. Pathway: credit snapshot. Scope: the business, operating model, ownership, control, transactions and sponsor and governance behaviour of the issuer, from the supplied annual reports, quarterly reports and results releases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earlier module output used by this module:

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance risk to creditors is medium: a majority stockholder controls Comstock and has put capital in rather than taken it out since 2024, but the 2026 plan leans on partner capital and a pending asset sale whose terms are only partly disclosed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Comstock is a single-basin natural gas producer, so the creditor case rests on gas prices and on how much cash stays inside the borrowing group. Outside capital now stands between creditors and part of that cash in two places: the midstream subsidiary, where a fund holds a 27% interest with a minimum return, and the wells covered by the August 2026 farmout with a stockholder partnership. The USD 1.65 billion sale to SOCAR, signed on 2026-11-04, is planned to repay the bank facility but has not closed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Control is concentrated and its current size is not established, which keeps governance risk from being rated low. The majority stockholder held 71% after market purchases in the third quarter of 2024, the latest figure stated, and the 2026 proxy statement that would update it, confirm formal board independence and describe how related-party deals are approved is not supplied. Three of the five directors are listed as outside directors, but creditors cannot check whether the farmout described below was reviewed by directors without an interest.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Owner behaviour since 2024 has supported creditors, with one open test. Entities controlled by the majority stockholder bought newly issued shares for USD 100.5 million in March 2024, no common dividend has been paid since 2023 and the bank facility restricts dividends and share repurchases. The test is the August 2026 farmout: a partnership owned by the stockholder pays 85% of the cost of 18 Western Haynesville wells and 80% of the cost of nine Legacy Haynesville wells, expected to cost about USD 450 million, and takes the net proceeds after Comstock recovers its costs until it earns a 15% return. That eases borrowing needs now and sends later cash flow from those wells to a related party, on terms not tested against an independent price in the documents supplied; the receivable from the stockholder partnerships has already risen from USD 3.6 million at 2025-12-31 to USD 51.5 million at 2026-09-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 101; 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A second layer of outside capital sits inside the midstream subsidiary and takes a share of its distributable cash, so not all of that cash is available to Comstock's creditors. In June 2026 a fund managed by Sixth Street Partners paid USD 600 million for a 27% interest in Pinnacle Gas Services, with a minimum annualised return, exit provisions and a step down to 19.5% after return hurdles; the cash redeemed the earlier partner for USD 445 million. Comstock keeps control through a management agreement and a majority of the board and consolidates the subsidiary, but USD 471.5 million of net property and USD 16.4 million of cash cannot be used for general corporate purposes, and the bank facility's collateral excludes the subsidiary.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is a single-commodity, single-basin gas producer with moderate customer concentration, so governance quality cannot offset price risk. Substantially all proved reserves are in the Haynesville and Bossier shales and 41% of them are developed, leaving an undeveloped balance that needs capital; three customers took 39% of 2025 sales; 70% to 75% of gas is sold on the first-of-month index and the rest at daily spot prices. The gas services line resells purchased gas and earns almost no margin: a margin of −3.20% of its revenue in FY2025 and 3.11% in the nine months to 2026-09-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation C3; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Spending runs ahead of operating cash flow, so the plan depends on partner capital, asset sales and bank borrowings rather than internal cash alone. Operating cash flow covered 47.88% of capital expenditures in the nine months to 2026-09-30, against 68.65% a year earlier; in the same nine months the issuer borrowed USD 1,047 million on its bank facility and repaid USD 507 million, and took USD 600 million of minority capital into Pinnacle Gas Services, of which USD 445 million repaid the earlier partner.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C5; calculation C8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The SOCAR sale and the bank amendment of 2026-11-04 could change the credit picture materially, but no supplied document measures the effect. The agreed price of USD 1.65 billion is subject to adjustments, has an effective date of 2026-07-01 and is expected to close by the end of 2026 subject to approvals; the issuer plans to use it to repay the bank facility, on which USD 800.0 million was drawn at 2026-09-30, and to retire part of the 2029 senior notes. The price is 2.06x the bank borrowings and would leave USD 850 million for the notes, which have principal of USD 1,623.88 million. The bank maturity moves from 2027-11-15 to 2028-11-15, and to 2031-11-15 after closing and debt repayment. A pro forma figure is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 100; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reporting quality supports monitoring but does not cover governance. The auditor gave unqualified opinions on the 2025 statements and on internal control over financial reporting and the issuer reports every quarter with a results release, but the chairman and chief executive roles are combined, and formal director independence, executive pay and related-party approvals sit in a document not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 72; 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 79; 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 75

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for lower risk is conduct. The majority stockholder added USD 100.5 million of equity in 2024 and bought shares in the market, the company has paid no dividend since 2023 and its bank facility restricts distributions. Third-party buyers have also paid for minority interests: a fund managed by Sixth Street Partners paid USD 600 million for 27% of the midstream subsidiary and SOCAR agreed to pay USD 1.65 billion for minority interests in upstream assets and Pinnacle Gas Services. If the sale closes and its proceeds repay the USD 800.0 million drawn on the bank facility and part of the 2029 notes, the debt reduction would offset the cash flow ceded to outside holders and the rating could move toward low, although the farmout and the minority capital in the subsidiary would remain.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 101; 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 30

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would worsen if a dividend resumed while the bank facility is drawn, if more wells were farmed out to stockholder partnerships, if the proxy statement showed that directors without an interest did not approve the farmout, if the sale failed to close or its proceeds went elsewhere, or if the unseen Pinnacle terms let the minority investor force an exit or take cash ahead of the parent. It would improve on evidence of independent approval of related-party agreements, Pinnacle terms that leave Comstock's share of cash unconditional, and a closing that is followed by repayment of the bank facility.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The majority stockholder is not named in the statements and its latest stake is from 2024; if the current holding is lower, or the person named in the exhibit index and the release is not the stockholder, the control assessment and the related-party reading of the farmout would change.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The farmout, Pinnacle Gas Services, indenture and SOCAR terms are described only in summaries, so the reading that the minority investor's return reduces cash available to creditors, and the reading that the farmout supports creditors, could each reverse once the agreements are seen.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Formal director independence, committee roles beyond the audit committee and related-party approvals are not available, so the medium rating could not be lowered on this evidence and could rise if the proxy statement shows no independent review.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The SOCAR sale and bank amendment came after the 2026-09-30 balance sheet, so the deleveraging reading rests on the issuer's stated plan, not on a measured result.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three transactions define the period. On 2026-11-04 Comstock agreed to sell SOCAR non-operated working interests in 15% of its Western Haynesville upstream interest, 20% of its other upstream interests and 15% of its interest in Pinnacle Gas Services for USD 1.65 billion, subject to customary adjustments, with an effective date of 2026-07-01 and closing expected by the end of 2026. SOCAR's Western Haynesville interest falls to 7.5% after five years and a 15% return, and the issuer expects a gain of USD 150 million to USD 250 million on closing. The issuer plans to repay the bank facility and retire part of its 2029 senior notes with the proceeds.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On 2026-06-15 Pinnacle Gas Services issued Class A-2 Units equal to a 27% interest to a fund managed by Sixth Street Partners for USD 600 million and used the cash to redeem the earlier partner's interest for USD 445 million; no gain or loss was recognised because Comstock kept control. On 2026-08-31 Comstock agreed a farmout with a partnership owned by its majority stockholder, under which the partnership funds 85% of 18 Western Haynesville wells and 80% of nine Legacy Haynesville wells expected to cost about USD 450 million, and Comstock recovers its costs from the wells' net revenues before the partnership takes the net proceeds until it earns a 15% return, after which 50% of the interest in the subject wells reverts to Comstock.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Comstock has issued no notes since the USD 400.0 million of 2029 senior notes sold in April 2024. In the nine months to 2026-09-30 it borrowed USD 1,047 million on its bank facility and repaid USD 507 million, leaving USD 800.0 million drawn. The amendment of 2026-11-04 extends the bank maturity to 2028-11-15, with a further extension to 2031-11-15 after the SOCAR closing and debt repayment, and commitments stay at USD 1.5 billion. The subsidiary's own facility of USD 150 million was undrawn at 2026-09-30.

fields.value: Comstock is a gas-only Haynesville producer whose spending runs well ahead of operating cash flow, so its credit profile is average at best and rests on a pending asset sale; creditors should size leverage at the normalised 3.49x, not the reported 2.37x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt rose from USD 2,785.14 million at 2025-12-31 to USD 3,338.34 million at 2026-09-30, and the pro forma figure after the sale agreed on 2026-11-04 is not established. The sale price of USD 1.65 billion and a bank maturity now in 2028 limit near-term refinancing risk, but nothing yet shows spending falling to the level of cash flow, which is why the profile stays average.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Internal cash generation does not fund the investment plan, and that is the central weakness. Capital expenditures were 1.97x operating cash flow in the twelve months to 2026-09-30 and 1.50x in FY2025, and the 2026 plan of USD 1.4 billion to USD 1.5 billion for development and exploration is 1.65x to 1.77x that twelve-month operating cash flow, before USD 100 million to USD 150 million planned for the midstream partnership. Bank borrowings, asset sales and partner capital have met the gap, so debt rises whenever prices do not.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 63; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported leverage flatters credit quality. Net debt to twelve-month EBITDA is 2.37x as reported but 3.49x after removing sale gains and unrealised hedge gains, which sits just below the bank facility's leverage covenant of 3.5x; the covenant definition is not supplied, so no headroom is inferred. Net debt rose from USD 2,785.14 million at 2025-12-31 to USD 3,338.34 million at 2026-09-30, and pro forma net debt after the sale agreed on 2026-11-04 is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest cover is adequate and rate exposure is small. EBITDA covers cash interest 6.71x as reported and 4.55x on the normalised basis, and only the USD 800.0 million of bank borrowings carries a floating rate, 23.61% of debt principal, while the 2029 and 2030 senior notes carry fixed coupons.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and refinancing risk are manageable until 2028 but rest on one bank facility. At 2026-09-30 cash was USD 18.63 million and undrawn commitments were USD 700.0 million of USD 1,500.0 million, and pro forma figures after the sale of 2026-11-04 are not established. The amendment of that date moved the bank maturity from 2027-11-15 to 2028-11-15, and no other debt falls due before 2029, when USD 1,623.88 million of notes mature, followed by USD 965.0 million in 2030. The issuer's own fair values put the 2029 notes at 99.5% of face and the 2030 notes at 95%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business risk is concentrated in one commodity and one basin, so margins follow the gas price. A 60.10% rise in the realised gas price between FY2024 and FY2025 lifted normalised EBITDA by 21.97% even though output fell 14.67%, and normalised net leverage moved from 3.53x to 2.73x. Cash costs of USD 0.83 per Mcfe are 26.95% of the nine-month 2026 realised price, which leaves room at current prices, but a 10% lower price on twelve-month sales would cut normalised EBITDA by 14.59% and lift normalised net leverage to 4.09x before hedge gains and any cost response.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 58; EX99.1_2026-09-30_crk_crk-ex99-1-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance risk is medium and does not change the credit view by itself. The majority stockholder has supplied equity and paid no dividend since 2023, but the August 2026 farmout with a stockholder partnership and a minority investor in the midstream subsidiary route part of future cash flow to outside holders, and the terms of both are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The sale to SOCAR is the swing factor, and its effect cannot yet be measured. The USD 1.65 billion price is 2.06x the USD 800.0 million drawn on the bank facility and equals 49.43% of net debt at 2026-09-30, and the issuer plans to repay the bank facility and retire part of the 2029 notes, but closing is expected only by the end of 2026 and no source states net debt or the earnings of the interests sold. Until it closes, creditors should rely on the normalised 3.49x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 30; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case for a better credit is asset quality and flexibility. Production costs were 36.87% of the realised price even in FY2024 when the price fell to USD 1.98 per Mcf, the issuer describes most capital spending as discretionary and cut it by 22.99% in FY2024, swaps and collars for 2027 equal about 41.88% of annualised 2026 volume with floors near USD 3.50 per MMBtu, and outside buyers have priced the assets: SOCAR agreed USD 1.65 billion and a fund paid USD 600 million for 27% of the midstream subsidiary. Against that, the cut in FY2024 was followed by a 14.67% fall in FY2025 output, and proved undeveloped reserves rose about fourfold in 2025 largely because the higher price in 2025 allowed locations to be booked, so asset coverage moves with the same gas price.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C2; calculation C4; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if the sale closes, its proceeds repay the bank facility and part of the 2029 notes, and capital spending is held near operating cash flow, which would move normalised leverage back toward the 2.73x of FY2025. It would worsen if the gas price falls back toward the FY2024 level with spending unchanged, if the sale fails or its proceeds are redirected, which would leave the bank maturity in 2028 and the 2029 notes 106 days apart, or if the covenant definition proves tighter than the normalised measure used here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No rating, peer set or market quote is supplied, so the profile cannot be compared with other gas producers and the label average rests on the issuer's own figures; a weaker peer group would raise the label, a stronger one would lower it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No forecast or scenario assumptions are supplied, so the downside is a sensitivity on reported twelve-month figures, not a projection, and it cannot say when liquidity would tighten.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Maintenance spending and decline rates are not disclosed, so the share of capital spending that is truly discretionary rests on the issuer's statement and the FY2024 cut, and the cash-flow weakness could be larger or smaller than shown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The consolidated figures include a midstream subsidiary whose cash and assets Comstock cannot use freely, and no figures for the group that borrows under the bank facility are supplied, so leverage as the bank lenders see it may differ from the figures used here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Unit costs are low against the realised price, which keeps margins positive in weak price years. Cash costs were USD 0.83 per Mcfe in the nine months to 2026-09-30, 26.95% of the realised price, and the issuer states an operating margin of 73%; in FY2024 production costs of USD 0.73 per Mcfe were 36.87% of a USD 1.98 price. Margin therefore moves with price rather than cost, which supports cash generation through a price trough.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_crk_crk-ex99-1-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 59; calculation C2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital spending is largely discretionary, which gives management a lever to protect liquidity. The issuer states that the timing of most future capital expenditure is discretionary because it has few long-term commitments, remaining drilling rig commitments are USD 12.7 million, and capital expenditures were cut 22.99% in FY2024. The lever protects liquidity before it protects earnings, because output was 14.67% lower in FY2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C1; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The reserve base and operatorship give a long runway and control over timing. About 41% of proved reserves are developed, the reserve life is about 16 years and the issuer operates 99% of proved reserves, so it sets drilling pace and cost; the proved undeveloped volume is price-sensitive, however, because it rose about fourfold in 2025 on the higher gas price used to book it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt is long-dated and mostly fixed-rate. The bank facility matures on 2028-11-15 and the notes in 2029 and 2030, only 23.61% of principal floats, and swaps and collars cover volumes through 2028, so a price or rate shock reaches cash flow slowly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation is the first weakness. Capital expenditures were 1.97x operating cash flow in the twelve months to 2026-09-30, so debt, asset sales or partner capital fund the plan and net debt rose to USD 3,338.34 million at 2026-09-30, with the pro forma figure after the sale of 2026-11-04 not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Price exposure is the second weakness. The business sells one commodity from one basin at index prices, and a 10% lower price on twelve-month sales would cut normalised EBITDA by 14.59% and lift normalised net leverage to 4.09x before hedge gains and any cost response.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity rests on one bank facility. Undrawn commitments were USD 700.0 million at 2026-09-30, which would cover about 10.26 months of the twelve-month shortfall between operating cash flow and capital expenditures if no partner capital or sale proceeds arrived, and the extension of the bank maturity to 2031 depends on the sale closing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Outside holders hold claims on part of the cash flow. A fund holds a 27% interest in the midstream subsidiary with a minimum return, a stockholder partnership will take later cash flow from 27 wells under the August 2026 farmout, and a majority stockholder controls the vote, so consolidated figures overstate the cash that reaches Comstock's own creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Legal terms are unseen. The rank and security of the notes, guarantors, covenant definitions and the terms of the sale are not supplied, so creditor priority and covenant headroom are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Comstock produces natural gas almost entirely from the Haynesville and Bossier shales of North Louisiana and East Texas and operates 99% of its proved reserves, so it controls drilling pace and cost. Revenue is gas sales plus a gas services line that resells purchased gas and earns almost nothing, at 22.53% of FY2025 revenue and a margin of −3.20% of that revenue. The business therefore carries one commodity, one basin and one regulatory setting, which concentrates cash-flow risk in the gas price.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 59; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A majority stockholder, not named in the statements, held 71% when last stated in 2024, and no dividend has been paid since 2023. The midstream subsidiary is consolidated but a fund holds a 27% interest, and the August 2026 farmout puts a stockholder partnership beside Comstock in 27 wells. These structures move part of the cash flow to outside holders and reduce the weight creditors can place on the consolidated figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is set by price and only partly predictable. Output was 14.67% lower in FY2025 and 1.68% lower in the nine months to 2026-09-30, with the third quarter of 2026 9.47% higher than the third quarter of 2025, while the realised price moved from USD 1.98 per Mcf in FY2024 to USD 3.17 in FY2025 and USD 3.08 in the nine months of 2026 against USD 3.13 a year earlier. Between 70% and 75% of gas is sold at the first-of-month index and the rest at daily prices, three customers took 39% of 2025 sales and the issuer states that other purchasers could replace them, and there is no long-dated fixed-price sales book beyond swaps and collars. Revenue is cyclical, price-set and moderately concentrated, not contracted.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 22; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are defended by unit costs but not by contracts. Cash costs of USD 0.83 per Mcfe leave a wide gap to the realised price, and the issuer's operating margin of 73% reflects it, but gathering and transportation commitments of USD 85.4 million in 2026 and firm transportation of about 1.7 Bcf per day do not fall with output. Cutting drilling reduces capital spending rather than operating cost, so volume pressure would raise unit costs before it reduced them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is high and free cash flow is negative. Capital expenditures were 1.50x operating cash flow in FY2025 and 1.97x in the twelve months to 2026-09-30, no dividend is paid, and the tax provision in the nine months to 2026-09-30 was almost entirely deferred, which keeps cash taxes close to zero; federal tax losses of USD 1.5 billion, of which USD 740.6 million are expected to expire unused, shelter taxable income. EBITDA therefore does not turn into free cash flow at present: interest is paid from operating cash flow, but the capital programme beyond it is funded from borrowings and partner capital rather than from retained cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry limits pricing power: the issuer competes for properties and leases with larger companies and sells at index prices, so it is a price taker and its margin depends on its cost position. Barriers to entry are real but are about acreage and capital: years of leasing built the Western Haynesville position, and a new entrant would have to buy it. Substitutes matter on the demand side: the issuer names competing fuels as a market factor and cites LNG exports, exports to Mexico, petrochemicals and power generation as demand support, none of which is contracted in the supplied documents. Buyers are few at the top but replaceable at an index price, and suppliers hold some power through rig and midstream commitments that run for years, which reduces cost flexibility if volumes fall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: PEST factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the provided materials.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the SOCAR proceeds if applied to debt, continued well results in the Western Haynesville area, which the issuer reports as successful in its 30 wells to date, and growth in Gulf Coast gas demand. Threats that could weaken it are a gas price near the FY2024 level, floating-rate exposure on the bank debt, claims of outside holders on subsidiary and well cash flow, and the 2028 bank maturity if the sale does not close.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The supports are a low unit cost position, discretionary capital spending, long-dated mostly fixed-rate debt and a long reserve life. The constraints are negative free cash flow, normalised net leverage of 3.49x against a 3.5x covenant whose definition is not supplied, one bank facility behind liquidity and outside claims on cash. The trend is mixed: normalised net leverage fell 0.80x between FY2024 and FY2025 and has since risen 0.76x, so the 2025 improvement has reversed, while reported leverage of 2.37x hides that. The missing datapoints are covenant definitions, figures for the group that borrows under the bank facility, maintenance spending, ratings and pro forma figures after the sale of 2026-11-04.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the plan is to grow output with capital spending of USD 135 million to USD 155 million still to come in the fourth quarter of 2026, to close the SOCAR sale by the end of 2026 and to use the proceeds on debt. Output was 9.47% higher in the third quarter than a year earlier and the issuer expects production to increase in 2026. The bank maturity of 2028-11-15 is 728 days from the as-of date unless the extension to 2031 takes effect on closing and repayment, and the 2029 notes mature 834 days from the as-of date, so the refinancing question arises inside the horizon only if the sale does not close.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 58; EX99.1_2026-09-30_crk_crk-ex99-1-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C7; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the maturity wall of the bank facility, the 2029 notes and the 2030 notes is the main test, supported by a reserve life of about 16 years and the issuer's plan to fund activity mainly from operating cash flow. Tailwinds are Gulf Coast demand from LNG exports, exports to Mexico and petrochemicals and the data-centre power partnership, which the issuer describes in its own words without terms. Headwinds are price volatility, a minority holder's minimum return in the midstream subsidiary, floating-rate exposure on the bank debt and spending above cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is a gas price that falls back toward the USD 1.98 per Mcf of FY2024 while the sale does not close and the 2026 plan continues. The first operational break is operating cash flow, which already covered only 47.88% of capital expenditures in the nine months to 2026-09-30. A 10% lower price on twelve-month sales of natural gas and oil removes about USD 139.37 million, cutting normalised EBITDA by 14.59% and lifting normalised net leverage from 3.49x to 4.09x, above the 3.5x covenant level if its definition resembled the normalised measure, which is not known. Undrawn commitments of USD 700.0 million would cover about 10.26 months of the twelve-month funding gap of USD 818.81 million if no partner capital or sale proceeds arrived, and the 2028 bank maturity would then fall 106 days before the 2029 notes. Management would cut drilling, as in FY2024, which protects liquidity at the cost of output. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis only if the sale closes or spending is cut toward cash flow; no default is assumed. The observable triggers are undrawn commitments, quarterly capital expenditures against operating cash flow and the closing of the sale.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_crk.htm.jsonl, page 58; calculation C3; calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Comstock presents an average business profile supported by low unit costs, discretionary capital spending and long-dated debt, but credit quality is constrained by spending that runs ahead of operating cash flow and normalised leverage near the covenant level. Cash-flow durability appears weak at present because free cash flow is negative and follows the gas price. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the closing of the SOCAR sale and the use of its proceeds, with the notes valued at 95% to 99.5% of face on the issuer's own fair values. The primary downside path is a lower gas price with spending unchanged and the sale not closed. Further analysis would require the covenant definitions, figures for the bank borrowing group and the sale's closing statement. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: spending above operating cash flow while the asset sale is unclosed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crk.htm.jsonl, page 32
